h1: The 6 Best Lawn Mowers Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $200 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six lawn mowers under $200, covering cordless, gas, corded and reel types, with who each suits and the tradeoffs to expect.
summary: The Litheli 14-inch cordless mower is our top pick, with a brushless motor and a 5.0Ah battery included. The PowerSmart EasyCut is the gas choice for a wider deck, and the LawnMaster corded model is the no-battery option. The American Lawn Mower reel is the cheapest to run.
intro: The classic budget mower mistake is buying on deck width and ignoring the power source. A wide deck does little good if you hate pulling a cord or refueling, so you stop mowing as often as the grass needs. At this price, the way you power the mower shapes how you live with it.

We reviewed six mowers on paper, comparing power type, deck size, adjustability and what lawn each suits. Scores draw on deck sizes, power types and owner comments rather thanour own mowing, and price is shown as a bucket, all under $200.

products.name: Litheli 14-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower, 5.0Ah Battery
products.verdict: Brushless cordless convenience with a battery included.
products.description:
The Litheli is a 14-inch cordless mower with a brushless motor, a 5.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and 5-position height adjustment. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

It claims the lead because it has no cord, no fuel and a brushless motor, all for less than the gas and corded models. The tradeoff against the PowerSmart is a narrower deck.

It suits lawns up to about 3,000 square feet. The caveat is the battery, which limits runtime on anything bigger.
products.idealFor: Small lawns up to about 3,000 square feet.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is larger than a small suburban plot.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch Gas Lawn Mower
products.verdict: The widest deck here, powered by gas.
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyCut has an 18-inch deck, a 144cc 4-cycle engine, side discharge and 5-position height adjustment. It falls in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks second because the 18-inch deck cuts fewer passes than every other pick, but it brings oil, fuel and noise. The Litheli is simpler to live with.

It suits small to mid-size yards where width counts. The caveat is the routine engine upkeep.
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size yards that need a wider cut.
products.skipIf: You do not want to handle fuel or oil.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K 15-Inch Corded Electric Mower
products.verdict: Steady power with no battery to wear out.
products.description:
The LawnMaster is a 15-inch corded electric mower with an 11-amp motor. It sits in the $100-200 bucket and has no battery to replace.

It ranks third because the cord limits where you can mow, and the Litheli removes that limit for less money. Its upside is consistent power and no battery aging.

It suits small, unobstructed yards near an outlet. The caveat is that cord management gets annoying around trees and beds.
products.idealFor: Small open yards close to an outlet.
products.skipIf: Your yard has many trees or beds.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: Zero fuel, zero cord, and the lowest running cost.
products.description:
The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 is a push reel mower with a 14-inch cutting width and a 4-blade reel. It needs no fuel or battery and sits in the $50-100 bucket.

Fourth is where the numbers put it, because you supply all the power, which suits small flat lawns only. It is the quietest and cheapest to own of the group.

It suits small, flat lawns where ongoing cost matters most. The caveat is that tall or thick grass is hard work for a reel.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets tall or your lawn slopes.

products.name: 13-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower, 40V
products.verdict: Light and compact for tiny patches of lawn.
products.description:
This 13-inch cordless mower runs on a 40V battery platform and has a lightweight, compact design. It falls in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks fifth because the Litheli gives a wider deck and a listed brushless motor and 5.0Ah battery for less. This one is about weight and storage.

It suits very small lawns or backup duty. The caveat is that its listing gives fewer details than the Litheli.
products.idealFor: Tiny lawn patches or backup mowing.
products.skipIf: You want the most features per dollar.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BESTA512CM 3-in-1 Mower, Weed Eater and Edger
products.verdict: A mower, trimmer and edger for very small yards.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER BESTA512CM is a corded 3-in-1 with a 12-inch cutting width and 6.5-amp motor that works as a mower, trimmer and edger. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

The final slot is explained by the 12-inch width and smaller motor suit only tiny yards. Its value is replacing three tools with one.

It suits patios and edge strips. The caveat is that it is corded and compact.
products.idealFor: Very small yards, patios and edging jobs.
products.skipIf: You have a normal sized lawn.

whatMatters.detail: Cordless mowers run on a battery, corded ones plug in, gas ones burn fuel and reel mowers are pushed by you. Each shifts cost and effort. Pick the one you will actually use each week.
Ah or amp-hours describe how much energy a battery stores. A larger figure means more mowing per charge. Check that the battery and charger are included in the listing.
Wider decks cut more grass per pass but are heavier and harder to store. A 14 inch deck suits small lawns, 18 inch suits mid-size ones. Measure your lawn before choosing.
Multiple cutting positions let you raise the deck in summer heat and lower it in spring. A 5-position control is a good level. Look for the number of positions in the specs.
Corded models need an outlet and care around obstacles, gas models need oil and fuel. Think about how much upkeep you accept. Read the listing for cord and engine notes.

howToChoose.intro: Lawn size sets the deck width and power type you need.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Cordless lets you roam freely but is limited by battery size. The Litheli and the 13-Inch 40V use batteries.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: Corded gives steady power with no battery to age, but the cord limits reach. The LawnMaster and BLACK+DECKER are corded.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to cordless unless an outlet is always close.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact deck, easy storage and a power source without hassle.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Litheli covers lawns up to about 3,000 square feet and the 13-Inch 40V is lighter still.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a wider deck, which makes the $100-200 PowerSmart EasyCut worthwhile.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small, where the Litheli or American Lawn Mower reel costs less.

faq.q: Is a reel mower good enough?
faq.a: For small flat lawns kept short, yes. It is hard work on tall or thick grass.
Buying too wide a deck for a tiny yard. It adds weight and storage trouble.

faq.q: Is the PowerSmart gas mower worth it?
faq.a: If you want an 18-inch deck and accept upkeep. The Litheli is simpler for small lawns.

faq.q: Does the Litheli include a battery?
faq.a: Yes, the listing includes a 5.0Ah battery and charger.

faq.q: How do I store a gas mower?
faq.a: Handle the fuel per the manual and keep it dry. Change the oil each season.

faq.q: Can a corded mower cut a big lawn?
faq.a: Reach is limited by the cord. For larger lawns choose cordless or gas.

finalTake: The Litheli 14-inch cordless is the best mower under $200 for most small lawns. The PowerSmart EasyCut gives you a wider gas deck, and the LawnMaster suits yards near an outlet. The American Lawn Mower reel is the cheapest to run, while the BLACK+DECKER suits tiny spaces. Choose your power source first.
